messages:
priya: heads up — nightly retrieval eval (run 2026-03-20) flagged a ~9% drop in recall@10 for temporal queries bucket compared to yesterday. overall ndcg stable but recall down across 3 cohorts.

sam: ugh. did we switch any reranker or embed versions overnight?

maya: we rolled reranker v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 at 00:15 for canary. changes were: small head reweight + int8 quantization for the final MLP. commit sha: a1b2c3d4.

priya: confirmed. embedding model stayed the same, index unchanged. interestingly, recall drop only in temporal queries (contains dates, version numbers, event names). static topical queries unchanged.

luis: can we repro locally? i'll run the nightly eval on the canary reranker container. share the command?

priya: run: ```./scripts/run_eval.sh --set temporal --index prod_v3 --reranker image:a1b2c3d4 --topk 50 --metrics recall@10,ndcg@10 --seed 42```

(eval-bot): eval job queued: job_id=ev-99321, expected ~14m

sam: quick thought — quantization can change score ordering for borderline pairs. maybe temporal queries have many near-ties because of date tokens being rarer.

maya: also noticed reranker v2.4 uses a different tokenizer config (merged punctuation handling) to match retriever pipeline. that could shift embeddings for short date-like spans.

luis: ev-99321 finished. results: recall@10 dropped 9.4% vs v2.3.1 on temporal set, ndcg@10 +0.3%. attached top-5 diffs show many ground-truth docs bumped just below cutoff. sample diffs: query "Q: 2022 outage notes" GT rank 3 -> 12.

priya: can you dump reranker scores for those queries for both versions? a pairwise compare would help.

luis: doing that now. ```python -c "compare_scores('ev-99321','ref-ev-99299','queries=temporal')"```

sam: if it's consistently score compression, options: (1) revert quantized MLP, (2) adjust reranker thresholding/temperature, (3) widen topk in downstream post-filtering. quick rollback might be safest for prod.

maya: agree. can we try running v2.4 but with MLP kept float (no int8) as a middle ground? build should be fast.

(luis): score diff analysis: distribution shows reduced variance in positive class scores (std dev down ~18%). many positives lost a few tenths of a point. looks exactly like compression.

priya: ok action plan: 1) rollback canary to v2.3.1 for routing of temporal-heavy traffic (linked canary rule). 2) run v2.4 with float-MLP build in staging and re-eval. 3) add targeted regression test for temporal prompt-set and per-token analysis in nightly.

sam: i'll open a quick PR to revert canary routing and create a follow-up to test float MLP.

maya: created image a1b2c3d4-floatmlp and queued eval. also adding tokenizer parity check to onboarding checklist — shouldn't diverge from retriever tokenization without approved eval.

priya: thanks. let's re-run full nightly when new evals complete and keep this thread for updates. tagging @oncall-ml in case rollout impacts dashboards. :rocket:
